headline: Scaling Quantum Circuits, State Control, and Advantage
summary: Today's papers showcase key advances across quantum hardware, circuit theory, and advantage protocols. Highlights include constant-depth non-Abelian state preparation, high-speed neutral atom interconnects, and strict mathematical limits on circuit expressiveness and trainability.

themes.title: Scalable State Preparation & Interconnects
themes.body: Recent hardware breakthroughs tackle scaling bottlenecks: a constant-depth circuit prepares exotic non-Abelian FQH states on 156 qubits, while cavity-free atomic ensembles achieve remote entanglement rates matching two-qubit gate speeds.

themes.title: Expressiveness & Trainability in Shallow Circuits
themes.body: Theoretical studies reveal how internal mathematical structures govern shallow circuits: classical randomness significantly boosts generative expressiveness, whereas mathematical imaginarity sets strict limits on gradient trainability in QAOA.

themes.title: Quantum Advantage & Non-Hermitian Control
themes.body: Researchers demonstrate foundational quantum benefits, proving exact qutrit advantage in dimension-bounded zero-error communication games, and detailing momentum deformations for state purification via tunable exceptional points.

connections.body: 2608.05140 and 2608.05110 both leverage shallow quantum circuit depth to achieve complex state behaviors, using parallel local operations or classical randomness to overcome traditional circuit depth requirements.
